_comment: Roll-a-Day: Retirement Edition. The reader rolls a die for a morning plan (1-6) and again for an afternoon plan (1-6) and puts the two together: 36 possible days. Nobody checks the 36 pairings one by one, so every activity is held to one shape that makes any morning combine with any afternoon: about half a day or less, self-contained (never continuing or depending on the other half), no mealtime, no whole-day or overnight plan, and nothing belonging to the other half of the day (morningBanned / afternoonBanned) or to the evening (anySideBanned). No two activities on a page share a word of substance (softWords aside: who and where, not what), so no day doubles up. Variety is structural: each side takes six different kinds (the four coreKinds plus two extraKinds, the focus's boost first), every activity gets its own facet and flavour, shuffled by seed. A focus may bring its own facets for some kinds and drop flavours that contradict it, so the mix shows in what is printed, not only in a flavour the model may set aside: cosy keeps every kind close to home (a stroll round the block, a friend round for tea); out & about takes movement, learning and people out into town, leaving rest and making as the quieter ideas at home; creative turns the walk, the people and the home project creative; social puts company into movement, making, outings and play, leaving rest a quiet moment. exclusiveTerms keep the table open to everyone: nothing strenuous, no car, no golf course or beach house assumed. Idea shape, safety and meaning-level repeats reuse the Bucket List's gates (bucket-list/prompt.json).
